findings.issue: The value transcribes the contact email as 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu, as printed on the project site' — embedding source commentary inside the detail value. The bundle does print that misspelled address, so the address itself is grounded, but the parenthetical gloss is trust commentary that belongs in source_caveats, not in the descriptive field.

Five of six Creator objects use `principal_investigator` for individuals the bundle names only as 'Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team' members, not as principal investigators. Each carries a source_caveats admitting the slot is being used against its declared meaning. NIH RePORTER (tier 4) names exactly one PI, ROSENTHAL, ERIC S. Placing Bihorac, Jiang, Strekalova, Rashidi and Kwong in a `principal_investigator` slot asserts a role the bundle does not state for them.

`id` is set to https://chorus4ai.org/, which is also the value of `page`. The identifier for the dataset and the landing page for the project are the same URL, so the record's identity collapses into its web page; no distinct dataset identifier is attested in the bundle, but reusing `page` verbatim as `id` creates an ambiguous referent.

Set to true on the inference that PICU and NICU admissions imply minors. The bundle states the care settings but never characterizes any population as at-risk, and the accompanying source_caveats concedes no protections, assent or guardian consent are described. The boolean asserts a determination the bundle does not make.

Set to true by inference from the clinical nature of the data. The bundle never states a human-subjects determination for the dataset; the source_caveats itself notes IRB and compliance appear only as training-curriculum topics. The boolean is a regulatory characterization the evidence does not supply.

Jared Houghtaling is placed as `committee_contact` although the bundle names him only as one of two 'Request access' email contacts on the GitHub overview (tier 5), alongside dbold@emory.edu. No committee is named anywhere in the bundle, and the object's own source_caveats states 'The bundle names no formal data access committee'. Designating one of two access-request emails as a committee contact asserts a governance structure the evidence denies.

Massachusetts General Hospital is asserted as the accountable organization on the basis of being the NIH award recipient. The bundle states MGH is the awardee organization; it does not state that MGH is accountable for the data over time. The inference is recorded in source_caveats but the slot still carries the unattested claim.

Two instance entries describe overlapping imaging content with conflicting counts: instances[2] carries counts 7642 ('admissions with radiology data', tier 2) and instances[3] carries counts 1000 ('images available', tier 4). The units differ (admissions vs images), so these are not strictly contradictory, but emitting both as sibling Instance objects with the same data_substrate and data_topic reads as double-counting of the imaging modality.

Includes `OTHER` without any indication of which standard it stands for. The prose `conforms_to` names OHNLP, EDF+ and Persyst as the standards not covered by the enumerated terms, so the mapping is recoverable, but a bare `OTHER` in a queryable enum list conveys nothing on its own.

The note reproduces the website banner about administrative review. This is a statement about the source page's status rather than dataset content; under the digest's guidance it is trust commentary and fits source_caveats. It is also partially duplicated by the existing source_caveats treatment of the bundle's disagreements.

'Bridge2AI' is included as a keyword. The declared naming rule governs composed prose and this is a program name the bundle uses, so it is acceptable, but the keyword list mixes subject terms with a program affiliation, weakening its discovery value.
Omitted, correctly — the bundle states no recommended citation. Noted only to record that the omission was checked and is supported.

The scalar `license` slot is omitted while `license_and_use_terms.license_terms` and `ip_restrictions.restrictions` both discuss the MIT License applying to CHoRUS software repositories. The omission is correct — no license governs the data itself — but a reader comparing the two structured objects may expect the scalar to be populated; the distinction is carried only in prose.

The timeframe object carries only `timeframe_details` and leaves `start_date` and `end_date` empty, while the prose inside it states the funded project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. Those are award dates rather than data-collection dates, so leaving the date fields empty is defensible, but the prose then supplies dates the declared date slots do not carry.

Five DistributionFormat objects populate only `format` with a prose sentence describing the standard and its scope (e.g. 'OMOP Common Data Model tables for demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets (OMOP schema with extensions) and diagnoses'). `format` is intended for the format designation; `media_type`, `access_urls` and `download_url` are all absent because the bundle supplies none, leaving the objects thin and the format values overloaded with scope description.

`subpopulation_elements_present` is true but `distribution` is absent, and the object's own source_caveats states no distribution across subgroups is given. The object therefore asserts the presence of subpopulations while carrying no representation figures — supported by the bundle, but structurally near-empty.

Omitted although the bundle states '23 Tb' of waveform data. That figure covers only the waveform modality, not the whole dataset, so the omission is correct; the figure is preserved in instances[4].notes.

summary: The full record is broadly well grounded in the declared bundle and handles the released-size disagreement (50,000 vs 45K vs 100,000 admissions) correctly by preferring the tier-2 project documentation and recording the lower-ranked figures in source_caveats. No fabricated organization or person identifiers appear, no undeclared enum values are used, and multivalued slots emit one object per entity rather than collapsing them. The most serious defects are role and structure misassignments rather than invented content: five Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team members are recorded in `creators[].principal_investigator`, a slot whose meaning the bundle does not support for them, with each object's own source_caveats conceding the mismatch; one of two access-request email contacts is designated `data_governance.committee_contact` although the same object states no committee exists; and source commentary ('as printed on the project site') is embedded inside a maintainer detail value. Two booleans — `at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included` and `human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects` — assert determinations by inference from care setting and data type that the bundle never makes. `id` duplicates `page`, leaving the dataset without a distinct identifier. Remaining findings are low-severity shape and thinness issues: a bare `OTHER` in `conforms_to_standard`, banner text in `notes` that belongs in `source_caveats`, prose-overloaded `format` values, and structured objects (subpopulations, collection_timeframes) whose declared fields stay empty while their prose carries the content. All repairs belong in the full record; the core record is a projection and states nothing independently.
